The claim that appendix row k is Work_Envir_2.k_1 rests on presentation order plus the .sav ordinal. Corroborating structure, not proof: the appendix lists 6 Skills-development and 7 Work-life rows against .sav codes 3.2-3.7 and 5.1/5.2/5.4-5.8, i.e. it reproduces the RETAINED items in the original questionnaire's own numbering order, with the three dropped items (paper: 'three items were dropped due to small loadings ... one from skill development, one from work-life balance, and one from tangible employee involvement') simply absent. Work environment lost no item, so its five codes are contiguous 2.1-2.5 and the alignment is 1:1. (3) STEP 5b -- PARTIAL, see verify_avilatamayo_2022_work_envir.R. Route 9 is decisive on the option axis: all 35 item x level cell counts computed from the raw .sav match the live table exactly (e.g. 2.2_1: 38/40/42/83/78/90/62), so the 1..7 integers are the source's own codes unrecoded and the anchors attach in the source's order. Route 3 pins membership and rules out reverse-scoring: the five live items composite to M=4.7689, SD=1.3707, alpha=0.8776 against the paper's Table 1 Working environment 4.77 / 1.37 / .87 (n=431 complete). Route 8 is consistent but weak: the broadest claim (2.1, 'policies always provide a safe and healthy working environment') is the most endorsed at 5.162 and the most demanding (2.5, 'remove psychosocial hazards', 4.372; 2.2 ergonomic keypads, 4.480) the least. What is NOT established is the order of the five texts within the subscale -- the paper publishes no per-item statistic (Fig 2 is a second-order path diagram with seven factor loadings, Tables 1-3 are construct-level), and 2.3 and 2.4 have means 4.907 vs 4.910. A swap of those two would be undetectable here. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. (4) STEP 3b: the table is the right block. Live items are the five Work_Envir codes, resp 1-7, n=431-433 each, matching the appendix's five-row 'Entorno de trabajo' block; the paper's other six ICSR dimensions and the Meyer/Allen commitment scale are separate columns and separate IRW tables. The instructions paragraph is shipped exactly as printed including its unclosed parenthesis ('...7 = totalmente de acuerdo.') and its lowercase anchors; the Spanish option_text is those anchors as the instruction line spells them, not recapitalised. Item 1's English 'Our organization's policies' is the appendix's own wording and is not harmonised with the 'the company' phrasing of items 2-5. (7) DATA NOTE, not a text defect: the .sav contains a handful of non-integer cells (4.5671641, 4.525) which are the paper's stated mean-imputation for <2% missing data; the processing script drops them, which is why items 2.3 and 2.4 carry n=432 and n=431 against 433. The upstream instrument is Mory et al.'s ICSR Q, an academic scale carried in a journal article and not sold by a test publisher; a search for a licence, fee, permission-required or non-commercial statement for the ICSR Q found none to quote. instrument_rights_register.csv holds no row for this instrument or family. Silence is permission, so extracted normally; no register row written (a round may write `block`, never `ship`). Two conventions that will apply to them and are recorded rather than acted on: the appendix reproduces RETAINED items only, so skills_dev and work_life have a numbering gap (3.1, 5.3) that must be read off the .sav column names rather than counted off the appendix; and the appendix's last row in every other dimension is an 'Overall, the company...' summary item, which Working environment does not have. The one open item -- the within-subscale order -- is a determinate gap, not an access failure: the paper publishes no per-item statistic and the appendix numbers no row, so only new material from the authors or the Mory et al. original numbering could upgrade PARTIAL to VERIFIED.
